model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In browser pages, React and workers, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: host type of the declared primitive, checked by the compiled Lean constructor before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.context: React lifecycle on the browser main thread
model.conversionNote: JavaScript and TypeScript pass ordinary record objects. Host callbacks returning checked records require withRecovery(callback, value); recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected nested-field and record constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: proof-free JavaScript record objects validated by the selected constructors when passed to returned Lean closures; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. PHP-Wasm and native PHP require their own distinct archives. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.
model.meaning: A structure with zero or more runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices. A proof-only record crosses as an empty carrier and a Unit-bearing record keeps its unit field; neither is an absent, null or default value.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.
model.platform: Installed npm archive selected through a browser conditional export and bundled with Vite

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.context: React lifecycle on the browser main thread
model.conversionNote: JavaScript and TypeScript pass ordinary record objects. Host callbacks returning checked records require withRecovery(callback, value); recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected nested-field and record constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: proof-free JavaScript record objects validated by the selected constructors when passed to returned Lean closures; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Preserve the dependency through a checked lowering or a reviewed exclusion; never discard it as an implicit argument.
model.context: React lifecycle on the browser main thread
model.conversionNote: Pass the bound and Fin payload through the profile's ordinary Nat representation. The adapter enforces payload < the live earlier bound before Lean entry; no proof value crosses the host boundary.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the profile's ordinary Nat values for the bound and Fin payload; payload < the live earlier bound
limitations: The eleven same-run producer artifacts establish all thirty-four direct dependent-signature cells: seventeen supported profiles across ordinary Lean source and independently reviewed Binding IR.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: React lifecycle on the browser main thread
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In browser pages, React and workers, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: host type of the declared primitive, checked by the compiled Lean constructor before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: JavaScript and TypeScript pass ordinary record objects. Host callbacks returning checked records require withRecovery(callback, value); recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected nested-field and record constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: proof-free JavaScript record objects validated by the selected constructors when passed to returned Lean closures; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. PHP-Wasm and native PHP require their own distinct archives. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.
model.meaning: A structure with zero or more runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices. A proof-only record crosses as an empty carrier and a Unit-bearing record keeps its unit field; neither is an absent, null or default value.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.
model.platform: Installed npm archive selected through a browser conditional export and bundled with Vite
model.scope: Installed npm packages carry proof-free checked-record values through synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Node executes the JavaScript runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript consumers; strict TypeScript checks the generated declarations, and Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execute page, React and dedicated-worker consumers. model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: JavaScript and TypeScript pass ordinary record objects. Host callbacks returning checked records require withRecovery(callback, value); recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected nested-field and record constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: proof-free JavaScript record objects validated by the selected constructors when passed to returned Lean closures; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Preserve the dependency through a checked lowering or a reviewed exclusion; never discard it as an implicit argument.
model.conversionNote: Pass the bound and Fin payload through the profile's ordinary Nat representation. The adapter enforces payload < the live earlier bound before Lean entry; no proof value crosses the host boundary.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the profile's ordinary Nat values for the bound and Fin payload; payload < the live earlier bound
limitations: The eleven same-run producer artifacts establish all thirty-four direct dependent-signature cells: seventeen supported profiles across ordinary Lean source and independently reviewed Binding IR.

Every installed package checks a concrete Fin value against the live earlier Nat argument before entering Lean, exercises rejected endpoints and huge values, preserves caller data, and recovers for later calls.
The same-run receipt authenticates all forty-four independent checker summaries across eleven lanes, two author routes and full and result-only public APIs.
The native, managed, dynamic-language, browser, WIT/WASI and four-ABI Perl lanes use reproducible source-free package handoffs and public host APIs.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In browser pages, React and workers, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In browser pages, React and workers, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: C uses generated checked-record structs and callback recovery pointers; C++ uses generated value types and with_recovery. Recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply nested-field constructors before the enclosing record constructor. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: proof-free generated C structs or C++ value objects validated by the selected constructors when passed to returned Lean closures; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. PHP-Wasm and native PHP require their own distinct archives. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.
model.meaning: A structure with zero or more runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices. A proof-only record crosses as an empty carrier and a Unit-bearing record keeps its unit field; neither is an absent, null or default value.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. model.scope: Relocated ordinary-source Lean builds reproduce and install concrete C and C++ exports for finite generic specializations. Installed consumers exercise leading implicit type arguments, explicit type arguments, Lean-selected instance dictionaries at scalar and constructed types, and alias type arguments including an alias of Array UInt32, without access to the source tree; the unspecialized declarations stay absent. A generic structure instantiation named by an abbrev is admitted as an alias-named record; an unnamed one is rejected at the source with a classified diagnostic. A closed instantiation of a generic structure named by an abbrev is an alias-named record: the alias is its identity and Lean spelling, Lean instantiates every field and the constructor at the alias's arguments and universes, the Binding IR records the structure and its resolved arguments as the lean-lang.org/instantiation extension, and two aliases of one application are two host types with identical layout and the same origin. Source-free offline C and C++ consumers pass 1013 and 1012 checks over the alias-named records, including a phantom instantiation and the pair of two named instantiations. Installed packages also execute nine configured specializations over alias-named generic records, separate namespaces and List/Option aliases, alongside the ten direct record exports. Each alias keeps its name and compiler-recorded origin; host assignability follows the host language. The local Array supplement verifies Array-valued fields and arrays of alias-named records, alongside every original direct export and nine finite specializations. It covers ordinary-source native packages on glibc 2.36, not hosted release-floor acceptance or reviewed generic records.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: GMP mpz_t, const char and uint8_t spans or cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Preserve the dependency through a checked lowering or a reviewed exclusion; never discard it as an implicit argument.
model.context: C++20 over the generated C API
model.conversionNote: Pass the bound and Fin payload through the profile's ordinary Nat representation. The adapter enforces payload < the live earlier bound before Lean entry; no proof value crosses the host boundary.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the profile's ordinary Nat values for the bound and Fin payload; payload < the live earlier bound
limitations: The eleven same-run producer artifacts establish all thirty-four direct dependent-signature cells: seventeen supported profiles across ordinary Lean source and independently reviewed Binding IR.

Every installed package checks a concrete Fin value against the live earlier Nat argument before entering Lean, exercises rejected endpoints and huge values, preserves caller data, and recovers for later calls.
The same-run receipt authenticates all forty-four independent checker summaries across eleven lanes, two author routes and full and result-only public APIs.

Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: GMP mpz_t, const char and uint8_t spans or cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: GMP mpz_t, const char and uint8_t spans or cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: .NET and JVM use generated WithRecovery values; native PHP uses with_recovery(callback, value); WIT typed registration owns a copied recovery record. Recovery is checked before callback entry or application execution and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected record and nested field constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.

model.scope: Relocated ordinary-source Lean builds reproduce and install concrete .NET exports for finite generic specializations. Installed consumers exercise leading implicit type arguments, explicit type arguments, Lean-selected instance dictionaries at scalar and constructed types, and alias type arguments including an alias of Array UInt32, without access to the source tree; the unspecialized declarations stay absent. A generic structure instantiation named by an abbrev is admitted as an alias-named record; an unnamed one is rejected at the source with a classified diagnostic. Installed packages also execute nine configured specializations over alias-named generic records, separate namespaces and List/Option aliases, alongside the ten direct record exports. Each alias keeps its name and compiler-recorded origin; host assignability follows the host language. The local Array supplement verifies Array-valued fields and arrays of alias-named records, alongside every original direct export and nine finite specializations. It covers ordinary-source native packages on glibc 2.36, not hosted release-floor acceptance or reviewed generic records.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C#, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: Unit, bool, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, sbyte, short, int, long, BigInteger for Nat and Int, float, double, string, byte[], Rune, ulong for USize and long for ISize. Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: corresponding C# primitive value in generated sealed records and active case records across all nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal C# acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete NuGet packages from two author roots, remove author sources, restore offline, replay after relocation and execute again after deleting all consumer sources. The runs use .NET SDK 8.0.424 and shared framework 8.0.30 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Original packages, receipts, restore inputs, API-probe diagnostics, execution records and selected sources are retained; external toolchain binaries are represented by version, size and digest. Other hosts need their own primitive-base nominal acceptance. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. Hosted release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow; archived absolute paths describe the original local runs and are not CI prerequisites.

Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C#, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: Unit, bool, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, sbyte, short, int, long, BigInteger for Nat and Int, float, double, string, byte[], Rune, ulong for USize and long for ISize. Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: BigInteger, string and byte[], checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C#, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: Unit, bool, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, sbyte, short, int, long, BigInteger for Nat and Int, float, double, string, byte[], Rune, ulong for USize and long for ISize. Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: corresponding Java or Kotlin primitive value in generated records and sealed variant cases across all nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal JVM acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, nested Pair/Array/Option/Except values, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize with JDK 22.0.2 and Kotlin 2.2.0 through offline Maven-package installation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Java and Kotlin consumers run after relocation and again after removal of all consumer sources. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain pending. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured; local runs do not establish hosted 2.38 release-floor acceptance.

The installed generic-Subtype matrix covers the closed GenericNat alias of GenericCarrier Nat, its Positive field, retained Nat marker, distinct plusOne and plusTwo per-specialization constructor choices, and constructor-free copied results. It does not expose open generic host types, arbitrary type arguments or predicates, generic Fin fields, PHP-Wasm, callbacks, ownership, recursive generic graphs, dispatch cost or peak memory. The dependent foundation separately checks retained Nat, Bool and String indices in compiler and reviewed contracts; it does not infer installed host coverage for those dependent shapes. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned Subtype acceptance covers one selected Nat Subtype field in the tested acyclic Bundle, borrowed and transferred inputs, leased or retained results, rejection before ownership movement, exact cleanup and recovery through the named public package APIs. Recursive owned graphs, owned checked-record fields, owned callback positions, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. PHP-Wasm has separate owned-Subtype evidence and is not widened by this promotion. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: BigInteger, String and byte[] or BigInteger, String and ByteArray, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the base value projected from the proof-backed Lean result; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: BigInteger, String and byte[] or BigInteger, String and ByteArray, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.context: Kotlin calling the generated Java API
model.conversionNote: .NET and JVM use generated WithRecovery values; native PHP uses with_recovery(callback, value); WIT typed registration owns a copied recovery record. Recovery is checked before callback entry or application execution and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected record and nested field constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: generated proof-free record values checked by the selected constructor in returned-closure inputs; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: The generated contract covers synchronous copied-value callbacks, Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, admitted option/result/array containers and returned closures. Retained or asynchronous host callbacks, owned checked records, arbitrary indexed or recursive checked records, dispatch cost and memory bounds remain separate work.

Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.

model.context: Kotlin calling the generated Java API
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: BigInteger, String and byte[] or BigInteger, String and ByteArray, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Kotlin calling the generated Java API
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the base value projected from the proof-backed Lean result; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Kotlin calling the generated Java API
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: BigInteger, String and byte[] or BigInteger, String and ByteArray, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

Java and Kotlin consumers run after relocation and again after removal of all consumer sources. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain pending. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured; local runs do not establish hosted 2.38 release-floor acceptance.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the base value projected from the proof-backed Lean result; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

Primitive-base nominal JVM acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, nested Pair/Array/Option/Except values, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize with JDK 22.0.2 and Kotlin 2.2.0 through offline Maven-package installation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Java and Kotlin consumers run after relocation and again after removal of all consumer sources. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain pending. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured; local runs do not establish hosted 2.38 release-floor acceptance.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: JavaScript and TypeScript pass ordinary record objects. Host callbacks returning checked records require withRecovery(callback, value); recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected nested-field and record constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: proof-free JavaScript record objects validated by the selected constructors when passed to returned Lean closures; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. PHP-Wasm and native PHP require their own distinct archives. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.
model.meaning: A structure with zero or more runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices. A proof-only record crosses as an empty carrier and a Unit-bearing record keeps its unit field; neither is an absent, null or default value.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.
model.platform: Node 22 ESM with separate generated runtime and component npm archives
model.scope: Installed npm packages carry proof-free checked-record values through synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Node executes the JavaScript runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript consumers; strict TypeScript checks the generated declarations, and Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execute page, React and dedicated-worker consumers. Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 archives independently replay node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker ordinary and reviewed installed packages at the recorded release floor. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.

compilation.note: Compiled packages retain every runtime payload and refinement check while proof-only values have no ABI slot or allocation.

generation.note: Generated public APIs omit proof storage and proof arguments; they do not substitute null, Unit, a default value or fabricated evidence.

installedExecution.note: Installed consumers exercise direct proof parameters and proof-free signatures, retained field and callback positions, and the fail-closed refusal of proof-valued exports.

packaging.note: Both author routes produce receipt-closed prepared packages that install offline, relocate and replay after author and build removal.

model.absence: Erasure is determined by elaborated Lean types, not by substituting null for an unknown type.

model.failure: Keep runtime refinement checks and theorem provenance even when proof arguments are erased.
model.hostType: no runtime result; a proof-valued export is refused
limitations: The ten same-run producer artifacts establish ordinary and independently reviewed installed proof-parameter erasure and proof-free public signatures for all seventeen supported consumer profiles.
