model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: declared primitive's host value in copied record and variant fields across nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal npm acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. The observed consumers are Node 22.23.2/Linux x64 and strict TypeScript with wasm32 values. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce from two authors, install offline after author removal and replay after physical relocation. Complete package archives, original records, selected sources and runtime inputs are retained; external toolchain binaries are not. The local compiler uses the repository's Nix command transport adapter, not a Nix sandbox. Other hosts need their own primitive-base nominal acceptance. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. These local runs do not establish hosted acceptance of later revisions; archived absolute paths describe the original machine and are not CI prerequisites.

The installed generic-Subtype matrix covers the closed GenericNat alias of GenericCarrier Nat, its Positive field, retained Nat marker, distinct plusOne and plusTwo per-specialization constructor choices, and constructor-free copied results. It does not expose open generic host types, arbitrary type arguments or predicates, generic Fin fields, PHP-Wasm, callbacks, ownership, recursive generic graphs, dispatch cost or peak memory. The dependent foundation separately checks retained Nat, Bool and String indices in compiler and reviewed contracts; it does not infer installed host coverage for those dependent shapes. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned Subtype acceptance covers one selected Nat Subtype field in the tested acyclic Bundle, borrowed and transferred inputs, leased or retained results, rejection before ownership movement, exact cleanup and recovery through the named public package APIs. Recursive owned graphs, owned checked-record fields, owned callback positions, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. PHP-Wasm has separate owned-Subtype evidence and is not widened by this promotion. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: host type of the declared primitive, checked by the compiled Lean constructor before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: declared primitive's host value in copied record and variant fields across nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal npm acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. The observed consumers are Node 22.23.2/Linux x64 and strict TypeScript with wasm32 values. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce from two authors, install offline after author removal and replay after physical relocation. Complete package archives, original records, selected sources and runtime inputs are retained; external toolchain binaries are not. The local compiler uses the repository's Nix command transport adapter, not a Nix sandbox. Other hosts need their own primitive-base nominal acceptance. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. These local runs do not establish hosted acceptance of later revisions; archived absolute paths describe the original machine and are not CI prerequisites.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: host type of the declared primitive, checked by the compiled Lean constructor before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.conversionNote: Perl passes generated record objects and uses Runtime::Callback recovery for host callbacks returning checked records. model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Preserve the dependency through a checked lowering or a reviewed exclusion; never discard it as an implicit argument.
model.context: Native Perl XS; Linux x86-64; one process-wide Lean runtime
model.conversionNote: Pass the bound and Fin payload through the profile's ordinary Nat representation. The adapter enforces payload < the live earlier bound before Lean entry; no proof value crosses the host boundary.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the profile's ordinary Nat values for the bound and Fin payload; payload < the live earlier bound
limitations: The eleven same-run producer artifacts establish all thirty-four direct dependent-signature cells: seventeen supported profiles across ordinary Lean source and independently reviewed Binding IR.

Every installed package checks a concrete Fin value against the live earlier Nat argument before entering Lean, exercises rejected endpoints and huge values, preserves caller data, and recovers for later calls.
The same-run receipt authenticates all forty-four independent checker summaries across eleven lanes, two author routes and full and result-only public APIs.

installedExecution.note: Installed consumers exercise direct proof parameters and proof-free signatures, retained field and callback positions, and the fail-closed refusal of proof-valued exports.

packaging.note: Both author routes produce receipt-closed prepared packages that install offline, relocate and replay after author and build removal.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Native Perl XS; Linux x86-64; one process-wide Lean runtime
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: declared primitive's host value in generated blessed record and variant wrappers across nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal Perl acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete CPAN component and runtime archives from two authors. Perl 5.36.3 and 5.38.2, each threaded and unthreaded, install them offline after author removal as prebuilt-only and build-xs deliveries and replay after physical relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor. The four accepted selections ran serially under two frozen producer revisions and recorded per-run host-load admission ceilings of 6, 8, 8 and 12; the hosted default stays 6 and the disk and memory floors never changed. Original archives, receipts, control runs, preserved non-accepted launches and selected sources at both revisions are retained; external toolchain binaries are not. The Perl caller's check counts equal the Python caller's as a consistency check, not as borrowed evidence. Other hosts need their own primitive-base nominal acceptance. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. These local runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance; archived absolute paths describe the original machine and are not CI prerequisites.

The installed generic-Subtype matrix covers the closed GenericNat alias of GenericCarrier Nat, its Positive field, retained Nat marker, distinct plusOne and plusTwo per-specialization constructor choices, and constructor-free copied results. It does not expose open generic host types, arbitrary type arguments or predicates, generic Fin fields, PHP-Wasm, callbacks, ownership, recursive generic graphs, dispatch cost or peak memory. The dependent foundation separately checks retained Nat, Bool and String indices in compiler and reviewed contracts; it does not infer installed host coverage for those dependent shapes. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned Subtype acceptance covers one selected Nat Subtype field in the tested acyclic Bundle, borrowed and transferred inputs, leased or retained results, rejection before ownership movement, exact cleanup and recovery through the named public package APIs. Recursive owned graphs, owned checked-record fields, owned callback positions, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. PHP-Wasm has separate owned-Subtype evidence and is not widened by this promotion. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Native Perl XS; Linux x86-64; one process-wide Lean runtime
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Primitive base value checked by the named Lean constructor; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Native Perl XS; Linux x86-64; one process-wide Lean runtime
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Constructed subtype projected to its primitive base value; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Native Perl XS; Linux x86-64; one process-wide Lean runtime
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Primitive base value checked by the named Lean constructor; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Constructed subtype projected to its primitive base value; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.context: Ordinary NTS CLI with FFI; reviewed Alpha Zend extension; PHP_INT_SIZE = 8
model.conversionNote: .NET and JVM use generated WithRecovery values; native PHP uses with_recovery(callback, value); WIT typed registration owns a copied recovery record. Recovery is checked before callback entry or application execution and is never successful output. Returned Lean closures apply the selected record and nested field constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: generated proof-free record values checked by the selected constructor in returned-closure inputs; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: The generated contract covers synchronous copied-value callbacks, Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, admitted option/result/array containers and returned closures. Retained or asynchronous host callbacks, owned checked records, arbitrary indexed or recursive checked records, dispatch cost and memory bounds remain separate work.

External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

model.conversionNote: In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: corresponding native PHP primitive value in generated final readonly records and active variant cases across all nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal native PHP acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, nested Pair/Array/Option/Except values, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Ordinary NTS CLI with FFI; reviewed Alpha Zend extension; PHP_INT_SIZE = 8
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Brick\Math\BigInteger, string and Bytes, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Ordinary NTS CLI with FFI; reviewed Alpha Zend extension; PHP_INT_SIZE = 8
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the base value projected from the proof-backed Lean result; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Ordinary NTS CLI with FFI; reviewed Alpha Zend extension; PHP_INT_SIZE = 8
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Brick\Math\BigInteger, string and Bytes, checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Ordinary NTS CLI with FFI; reviewed Alpha Zend extension; PHP_INT_SIZE = 8
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the base value projected from the proof-backed Lean result; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.conversionNote: A host callback receives a proof-free generated Claim whose Ticket is borrowed for the call. Host callback replies require with_recovery(callback, value); nested fields and the exact selected record constructor validate recovery before callback entry and actual replies after return. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.context: Node and Chromium PHP-Wasm; PHP_INT_SIZE = 4; weak/strict callers; lazy and startup adapters
model.conversionNote: A host callback receives a proof-free generated Claim whose Ticket is borrowed for the call. Host replies and explicit recovery values run mkClaim; an invalid explicit recovery rejects before callback entry and is never replaced by automatic recovery. Returned Lean closures validate host Claim inputs and project proof-free Claim results. Use the generated readonly record class. Host callback replies require with_recovery(callback, value); nested fields and the exact selected record constructor validate recovery before callback entry and actual replies after return. Returned Lean closures validate host-produced record inputs before their body. Resource-bearing Claim values additionally retain the live Ticket owner for the synchronous call. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Generated proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner; generated proof-free readonly Interval, Weighted and owned Claim records at host callback arguments and returned-closure inputs, checked by their exact selected constructors when produced by the host; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: Hosted acceptance covers the fixture's closed Fin bounds and copied Interval and Weighted records in synchronous callbacks on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned callback values, open dependent refinements, recursive refined callbacks, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. External Lean, PHP, Composer, Chromium, Nix, Emscripten and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. limitations: Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed.

Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions.

Hosted PHP-Wasm value-index acceptance covers only the archived top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. The run covers weak and strict callers, embedded and Composer arrangements, startup and lazy loading in Node and Chromium on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1. Complete Composer, component and shared-runtime archives, receipts, reports, deployments, execution records, original workflow records and source closures are retained; external Lean, Nix, PHP-Wasm, Emscripten, Node, Chromium and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Other host targets require separate installed evidence.

Hosted zero-payload PHP-Wasm acceptance covers only the retained Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark fixtures at copied parameter and result sites in four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only packages. It does not promote checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, other zero-payload shapes or another host. External Lean, consumer-language, package-manager and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs.

This local evidence covers the tested acyclic Booking, Window and Claim shapes, the quota bound and synchronous callbacks only. It does not establish recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch counts, peak memory or hosted acceptance. The pinned PHP-Wasm runtime, browser and external compiler distributions remain trusted inputs represented by recorded identities.

Hosted dependent checked-record acceptance covers only the retained top-level copied DependentRecords.Dependent parameter and result sites, whose Fin bound field depends on the runtime bound field and whose proof is rebuilt by the selected mkDependent constructor. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Dependent fields of other kinds, nested or recursive dependent records, checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, open or opaque indices and zero-payload records remain unreviewed here. The PHP-Wasm cells are the shared result tracked by #1461 and are not inferred from native PHP. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. PHP-Wasm and native PHP require their own distinct archives. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.
model.meaning: A structure with zero or more runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices. A proof-only record crosses as an empty carrier and a Unit-bearing record keeps its unit field; neither is an absent, null or default value.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.

model.conversionNote: In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices. In the tested owned Bundle, PHP-Wasm exposes the refined Int payload as Brick\Math\BigInteger inside the generated Payload and Bundle classes while resource fields retain their generated Ticket owners. Borrowed calls validate without consuming the input. A transferred call validates the complete refinement tree first, so rejection leaves every resource owner usable; success consumes the original owner and returns a fresh lease. Results contain the Int payload but no proof field.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: corresponding PHP-Wasm primitive value in generated final readonly copied records, active variant cases, and the tested acyclic owned Bundle; no proof field; selected Subtype fields are checked at their declared public site before a transfer consumes any resource
limitations: Primitive-base nominal PHP-Wasm acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, nested Pair/Array/Option/Except values, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce the complete Composer API, npm component and npm shared-runtime archives from two author roots, remove author and build roots, install offline, and replay twelve Node and Chromium contexts per selection twice after relocation. Those contexts cover embedded and Composer Node installations and Chromium bundles with startup/lazy loading and weak/strict callers on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1, Node 22.23.2 and Chromium 152.0.7977.75. The runs use 32-bit machine words, a 2 GiB free/available-memory floor and an 8.0 host-load admission ceiling. Original packages, receipts, caller/compiler records, executions and selected sources are retained; external toolchain and browser binaries are represented by identity rather than copied. PHP consumer source remains required at runtime. The tested recursive variant, its transparent alias and nested Array/Option carriers admit selected checked Subtype constructors and Fin bounds. Refined callbacks, recursive checked records, dependent types, dispatch-counted execution and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. Hosted current-revision acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow; archived absolute paths describe the original local runs and are not CI prerequisites.

This evidence does not establish PHP-Wasm callback refinements, recursive owned graphs, other predicates, dispatch counts or peak memory. The pinned PHP-Wasm runtime, browser and external compiler distributions remain trusted inputs represented by recorded identities.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Node and Chromium PHP-Wasm; PHP_INT_SIZE = 4; weak/strict callers; lazy and startup adapters
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: null, bool, PHP int, Brick\Math\BigInteger, float, string or generated Bytes, checked and constructed by the selected Lean constructor across all nineteen tested primitive bases; also in generated structural containers, acyclic records and active variant cases; generated recursive Chain values also check the selected constructor at every present value field and the Fin 3 bound at every digit field, including aliases and nested Array/Option carriers
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Node and Chromium PHP-Wasm; PHP_INT_SIZE = 4; weak/strict callers; lazy and startup adapters
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: null, bool, PHP int, Brick\Math\BigInteger, float, string or generated Bytes, checked and constructed by the selected Lean constructor across all nineteen tested primitive bases; also in generated structural containers, acyclic records and active variant cases; generated recursive Chain values also check the selected constructor at every present value field and the Fin 3 bound at every digit field, including aliases and nested Array/Option carriers
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. They do not add nominal-field, refined callback-signature, owned-value, recursive or general dependent/generic support. These are local installed runs, not hosted release-floor results. Dispatch and memory are unmeasured in these unmodified packages; the separate annotated C probe is not evidence for other hosts. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.
model.conversionNote: Python, Ruby and Rust require with_recovery(callback, value) for host callbacks returning checked records. Recovery is validated before callback entry and is never successful output. Lean-produced callback arguments carry only record payload fields; returned Lean closures apply the selected record and nested field constructors before their body. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: generated proof-free record values checked by the selected constructor in returned-closure inputs; proof-free Claim with a live Ticket owner at synchronous host arguments and checked returned-closure inputs
model.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
limitations: The generated contract covers synchronous copied-value callbacks, the fixture's Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, admitted option/result/array containers and returned closures. Retained or asynchronous host callbacks, owned checked records, arbitrary indexed records, dispatch cost and memory bounds remain separate work.

Hosted callback checked-record acceptance covers synchronous copied Interval and Weighted records, the Weighted field's selected Nat Subtype, the fixture's option/result/array containers, host callback replies and inputs to returned Lean closures. Retained or asynchronous callbacks, owned records, arbitrary indexed or recursive records, dispatch cost, peak memory and PHP-Wasm remain separate work. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. limitations: Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed.

Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions.

Hosted Python value-index acceptance covers only the archived top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full wheels cover parameters and results; standalone result-only wheels cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. The run covers offline installation and relocated replay on CPython 3.11 and 3.12 on Ubuntu 24.04, Linux x64/glibc 2.39 with a glibc 2.38 wheel floor. Complete wheels, extracted packages, environment inventories, receipts, reports, original workflow records and source closures are retained; external toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Other host targets require separate installed evidence.

Hosted zero-payload Python acceptance covers only the retained Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark fixtures at copied parameter and result sites in four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only packages. It does not promote checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, other zero-payload shapes, PHP-Wasm or another host. External Lean, consumer-language, package-manager and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs.

Hosted dependent checked-record acceptance covers only the retained top-level copied DependentRecords.Dependent parameter and result sites, whose Fin bound field depends on the runtime bound field and whose proof is rebuilt by the selected mkDependent constructor. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Dependent fields of other kinds, nested or recursive dependent records, checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, open or opaque indices and zero-payload records remain unreviewed here. The PHP-Wasm cells are the shared result tracked by #1461 and are not inferred from native PHP. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned checked-record acceptance covers the tested acyclic Booking with its copied checked Window, and Claim with its Ticket resource and checked quota. Full packages cover borrowed and transferred inputs, leased results, synchronous host callbacks and returned Lean closures. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced Claim results without checked-input, transfer or callback metadata. This does not establish Grant or its nested Subtype, arbitrary owned containers, recursive owned graphs, retained or asynchronous callbacks, other predicates, dispatch cost or peak memory. PHP-Wasm and native PHP require their own distinct archives. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.
model.meaning: A structure with zero or more runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices. A proof-only record crosses as an empty carrier and a Unit-bearing record keeps its unit field; neither is an absent, null or default value.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.
model.platform: Python 3.11 or newer on x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.38 or newer through the generated wheel and native runtime adapter

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Python, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: None for Unit, bool for Bool, int for every integer and native machine word, float for Float32 and Float, str for String and Char, and bytes for ByteArray. Generated frozen dataclasses carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: declared primitive's host value in generated frozen record and variant dataclasses across nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal Python acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete wheels from two authors. CPython 3.11.16 and 3.12.14 install the same wheel offline after author removal and replay after physical relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor. Original wheels, receipts, process records, environment closures and selected sources are retained; external toolchain binaries are not. Other hosts need their own primitive-base nominal acceptance. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. These local runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance; archived absolute paths describe the original machine and are not CI prerequisites.

The installed generic-Subtype matrix covers the closed GenericNat alias of GenericCarrier Nat, its Positive field, retained Nat marker, distinct plusOne and plusTwo per-specialization constructor choices, and constructor-free copied results. It does not expose open generic host types, arbitrary type arguments or predicates, generic Fin fields, PHP-Wasm, callbacks, ownership, recursive generic graphs, dispatch cost or peak memory. The dependent foundation separately checks retained Nat, Bool and String indices in compiler and reviewed contracts; it does not infer installed host coverage for those dependent shapes. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned Subtype acceptance covers one selected Nat Subtype field in the tested acyclic Bundle, borrowed and transferred inputs, leased or retained results, rejection before ownership movement, exact cleanup and recovery through the named public package APIs. Recursive owned graphs, owned checked-record fields, owned callback positions, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. PHP-Wasm has separate owned-Subtype evidence and is not widened by this promotion. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Python, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: None for Unit, bool for Bool, int for every integer and native machine word, float for Float32 and Float, str for String and Char, and bytes for ByteArray. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor.
