model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Python, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: None for Unit, bool for Bool, int for every integer and native machine word, float for Float32 and Float, str for String and Char, and bytes for ByteArray. Generated frozen dataclasses carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Python, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: None for Unit, bool for Bool, int for every integer and native machine word, float for Float32 and Float, str for String and Char, and bytes for ByteArray. Generated frozen dataclasses carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: Constructed subtype projected to its primitive base value; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

Installed consumers exercise leading implicit type arguments, explicit type arguments, Lean-selected instance dictionaries at scalar and constructed types, and alias type arguments including an alias of Array UInt32, without access to the source tree; the unspecialized declarations stay absent. A generic structure instantiation named by an abbrev is admitted as an alias-named record; an unnamed one is rejected at the source with a classified diagnostic. model.scope: Relocated ordinary-source Lean builds reproduce and install concrete Ruby exports for finite generic specializations. Installed consumers exercise leading implicit type arguments, explicit type arguments, Lean-selected instance dictionaries at scalar and constructed types, and alias type arguments including an alias of Array UInt32, without access to the source tree; the unspecialized declarations stay absent. A generic structure instantiation named by an abbrev is admitted as an alias-named record; an unnamed one is rejected at the source with a classified diagnostic. Installed packages also execute nine configured specializations over alias-named generic records, separate namespaces and List/Option aliases, alongside the ten direct record exports. Each alias keeps its name and compiler-recorded origin; host assignability follows the host language. The local Array supplement verifies Array-valued fields and arrays of alias-named records, alongside every original direct export and nine finite specializations. It covers ordinary-source native packages on glibc 2.36, not hosted release-floor acceptance or reviewed generic records.

model.meaning: Arguments inferred during Lean elaboration.
model.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.
model.platform: Rust 2021 crate on x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.38 or newer and the packaged native runtime adapter
model.scope: Relocated ordinary-source Lean builds reproduce and install concrete Rust exports for finite generic specializations. Installed consumers exercise leading implicit type arguments, explicit type arguments, Lean-selected instance dictionaries at scalar and constructed types, and alias type arguments including an alias of Array UInt32, without access to the source tree; the unspecialized declarations stay absent. A generic structure instantiation named by an abbrev is admitted as an alias-named record; an unnamed one is rejected at the source with a classified diagnostic. Installed packages also execute nine configured specializations over alias-named generic records, separate namespaces and List/Option aliases, alongside the ten direct record exports. Each alias keeps its name and compiler-recorded origin; host assignability follows the host language. The local Array supplement verifies Array-valued fields and arrays of alias-named records, alongside every original direct export and nine finite specializations. It covers ordinary-source native packages on glibc 2.36, not hosted release-floor acceptance or reviewed generic records.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Rust, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: `()`, `bool`, matching fixed-width integers, `BigUint` for `Nat`, `BigInt` for `Int`, `f32`, `f64`, `String`, `Vec<u8>`, `char`, `u64` for `USize` and `i64` for `ISize`. Generated structs and enums carry owned record and active-variant fields; input functions borrow those aggregate values. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only crates. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: corresponding owned Rust base value in generated structs and active enum variants across all nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal Rust acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete crates from two author roots, authenticate fourteen offline dependencies, remove author sources, install offline, replay after relocation and execute again after deleting all consumer sources. The runs use Rust and Cargo 1.90.0 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Original crates, dependencies, receipts, execution records, the interrupted pre-fix launch and selected sources are retained; external toolchain binaries are represented by version, size and digest. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured. Hosted release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow; archived absolute paths describe the original local runs and are not CI prerequisites.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Rust, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: `()`, `bool`, matching fixed-width integers, `BigUint` for `Nat`, `BigInt` for `Int`, `f32`, `f64`, `String`, `Vec<u8>`, `char`, `u64` for `USize` and `i64` for `ISize`. Generated structs and enums carry owned record and active-variant fields; input functions borrow those aggregate values. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only crates.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: &BigUint, &BigInt, &str and &[u8], checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Rust, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: `()`, `bool`, matching fixed-width integers, `BigUint` for `Nat`, `BigInt` for `Int`, `f32`, `f64`, `String`, `Vec<u8>`, `char`, `u64` for `USize` and `i64` for `ISize`. Generated structs and enums carry owned record and active-variant fields; input functions borrow those aggregate values. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only crates.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the base value projected from the proof-backed Lean result; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Rust, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: `()`, `bool`, matching fixed-width integers, `BigUint` for `Nat`, `BigInt` for `Int`, `f32`, `f64`, `String`, `Vec<u8>`, `char`, `u64` for `USize` and `i64` for `ISize`. Generated structs and enums carry owned record and active-variant fields; input functions borrow those aggregate values. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only crates.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: &BigUint, &BigInt, &str and &[u8], checked by the exported Lean validator and constructed by the adapter before dispatch; also in generated structural containers; also in tested acyclic records and variants

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Rust, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: `()`, `bool`, matching fixed-width integers, `BigUint` for `Nat`, `BigInt` for `Int`, `f32`, `f64`, `String`, `Vec<u8>`, `char`, `u64` for `USize` and `i64` for `ISize`. Generated structs and enums carry owned record and active-variant fields; input functions borrow those aggregate values. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only crates.

Author roots are removed before offline installation; the unchanged public C caller is compiled once, its source is removed, and the resulting executable runs before and after moving the complete installed tree, giving two executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice packet value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Checked-record WIT/WASI acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic checked records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete WIT component archives from two author roots, remove author roots, install offline, compile one unchanged public C caller, remove its source, and execute it before and after physically relocating each installation. The compiler-free runs use Wasmtime 42.0.1 and wasm-tools 1.245.1 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor, 64-bit native machine words and a recorded 20.0 host-load admission ceiling. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. The archive retains complete handoff archives, extracted package records, receipts, installed inventories, execution records and both producer and verifier source closures. GCC, wasm-tools and Wasmtime remain trusted toolchain inputs. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the dedicated workflow. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Additional inherited wit acceptance: The wit installed lane authenticates the reviewed full inherited checked-record package selection for wit-wasi. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only WIT/WASI component packages. Complete packages are reproduced from two author roots, installed offline, exercised before and after relocation, and checked at a glibc 2.38 release floor. The generated C host requires its packaged native Lean component runtime; it is not a standalone WASI command. Complete archives, receipts, source-free inventories, caller binaries, execution records, TAP, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. Compiler, operating-system, wasm-tools, Wasmtime, and C toolchain distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed WIT/WASI behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive wit acceptance: The wit installed lane authenticates the reviewed recursive recursive checked-record selection for wit-wasi. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover self-recursive Packet and mutual Envelope/Step groups with Option and Array carriers. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested plusOne/plusTwo Nat Subtype constructors. Each package is a copied-graph WIT component whose native host forwards exact refinement diagnostics as the final Wasmtime error cause; callbacks, resources and owned positions remain separate work. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. Accepted cells come from serial attempts r2 and r3 at one frozen revision; r1 and the r2 reviewed-mutual cell refused on disk and load guards and are retained only as observations. These local Linux x64/glibc 2.36 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. The wit installed lane authenticates the reviewed mutual recursive checked-record selection for wit-wasi. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover self-recursive Packet and mutual Envelope/Step groups with Option and Array carriers. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested plusOne/plusTwo Nat Subtype constructors. Each package is a copied-graph WIT component whose native host forwards exact refinement diagnostics as the final Wasmtime error cause; callbacks, resources and owned positions remain separate work. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. Accepted cells come from serial attempts r2 and r3 at one frozen revision; r1 and the r2 reviewed-mutual cell refused on disk and load guards and are retained only as observations. These local Linux x64/glibc 2.36 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Independent owned checked-record acceptance adds the acyclic Booking/Window and Ticket/Claim forms only. Host-produced inputs use the selected mkWindow or mkClaim before ownership transfer or Lean entry; Lean-produced values omit proofs. Full packages also check synchronous host replies and returned-closure inputs, preserve rejected caller values and recover on later valid calls. Standalone result-only packages expose Claim results without input-constructor, transfer or callback metadata. Earlier composition limits still apply to those earlier fixtures.

model.scope: Relocated ordinary-source Lean builds reproduce and install concrete WIT/WASI exports for finite generic specializations. model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Wasmtime Component Model wrapper over an x86-64 native Lean host
model.conversionNote: In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: corresponding WIT primitive value in named record fields and active variant payloads across all nineteen tested bases; no proof field; the closed GenericNat record carries its proof-erased Positive value beside a retained Nat marker; the tested acyclic owned Bundle preserves this checked field beside explicit resource identities
limitations: Primitive-base nominal WIT acceptance covers the tested acyclic records, variants, aliases, nested Pair/Array/Option/Except values, mixed Fin guards and constructor-free results over Unit, Bool, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Nat, Int, Float32, Float, String, ByteArray, Char, USize and ISize on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor, Wasmtime 42.0.1 and wasm-tools 1.245.1, with 64-bit native machine words. Two independent author builds reproduce each archive. Author/build roots are removed before offline installation, and caller compilation inputs are removed before the identical executable runs and replays after relocation. Generated package sources remain installed. The Component Model adapter requires its native host and is not a standalone WASI command. Refined callbacks, owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain separate work. Constructor/source entry counts and memory are unmeasured; local runs do not establish hosted 2.38 release-floor acceptance. The archive retains original text members, compiled components, caller binaries and complete producer and control receipts, but not complete native archives or native libraries. Compiler and operating system distributions remain trusted.

The installed generic-Subtype matrix covers the closed GenericNat alias of GenericCarrier Nat, its Positive field, retained Nat marker, distinct plusOne and plusTwo per-specialization constructor choices, and constructor-free copied results. It does not expose open generic host types, arbitrary type arguments or predicates, generic Fin fields, PHP-Wasm, callbacks, ownership, recursive generic graphs, dispatch cost or peak memory. The dependent foundation separately checks retained Nat, Bool and String indices in compiler and reviewed contracts; it does not infer installed host coverage for those dependent shapes. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

Owned Subtype acceptance covers one selected Nat Subtype field in the tested acyclic Bundle, borrowed and transferred inputs, leased or retained results, rejection before ownership movement, exact cleanup and recovery through the named public package APIs. Recursive owned graphs, owned checked-record fields, owned callback positions, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. PHP-Wasm has separate owned-Subtype evidence and is not widened by this promotion. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Wasmtime Component Model wrapper over an x86-64 native Lean host
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the WIT value of each tested primitive base (the unit enum, bool, u8/u16/u32/u64, s8/s16/s32/s64, little-endian `list<u32>` Nat limbs, the signed Int limb record, f32/f64, string, `list<u8>` bytes, char, and u64/s64 for the 64-bit native USize/ISize), checked and constructed by the selected Lean constructor across all nineteen tested primitive bases; also in generated structural containers, acyclic records and active variant cases

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
model.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.
model.context: Wasmtime Component Model wrapper over an x86-64 native Lean host
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the corresponding WIT primitive value projected from the proof-backed Lean result across all nineteen tested bases; also in generated structural containers, acyclic records and active variant cases

model.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.

model.context: Wasmtime Component Model wrapper over an x86-64 native Lean host
model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the WIT value of each tested primitive base (the unit enum, bool, u8/u16/u32/u64, s8/s16/s32/s64, little-endian `list<u32>` Nat limbs, the signed Int limb record, f32/f64, string, `list<u8>` bytes, char, and u64/s64 for the 64-bit native USize/ISize), checked and constructed by the selected Lean constructor across all nineteen tested primitive bases; also in generated structural containers, acyclic records and active variant cases
limitations: The structural fixtures cover Nat, String and UInt8 Subtype leaves, mixed Fin, transparent aliases and one closed List specialization. Archives retain package digests and selected producer sources, not package binaries or a complete toolchain closure.

model.conversionNote: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.
model.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.
model.hostType: the corresponding WIT primitive value projected from the proof-backed Lean result across all nineteen tested bases; also in generated structural containers, acyclic records and active variant cases
